UX · Product Design · 2024
PLUR
Workspace Discovery App · SAE Institute Athens
01Product Description
What is it
The App
A mobile map app for finding and booking workspaces — primarily cafés — based on real-time availability, equipment, and amenities.
Target Users
Who It's For
  • Remote workers
  • Freelancers
  • Hybrid workers
  • Digital nomads
Core Features
What It Does
  • Map-based search & filters
  • Real-time availability
  • Equipment info
  • Seat booking
Problems Solved
Time wasted searching · Unknown availability · No reservation system · Unfamiliar city (nomads)
02Competitive Analysis
Direct
RWCAFÉ
Mobile & desktop app in Greece. Good usability. Ergonomics would improve with a more minimal design.
Indirect
TripAdvisor
Strong filtering and GPS. Booking available but no availability feature — the critical gap Plur addresses.
Indirect
Athinorama
Good filters but overloaded layout and heavy ads. No booking, no availability.
Key Opportunity
No competitor offers real-time workspace availability combined with booking. This is Plur's primary competitive advantage.
03User Research
Methodology
How We Researched
  • Remote interviews via Google Meet & Discord
  • Audio recordings + written notes
  • Users selected by work type & tech familiarity
Goals
What We Wanted to Know
  • How do users find workspaces today?
  • How do they make reservations?
  • What are their key frustrations?
04Key Findings
Finding 01
Timing & Frequency
Visits mainly in the afternoon, 2–3×/week, at least 4 hours. Combined with other activities.
Finding 02
Reviews & Discovery
Most don't consult reviews but want verified ones. Most use Google Maps to discover places.
Finding 03
Meetings vs Solo
Most workers go alone and don't want to socialise. Meeting users need more seats.
Finding 04
Immediate Needs
Quick workspace suitability check. Fast view of amenities and availability. Default to Starbucks for reliability.
Finding 05
Offers & Discounts
Some users want personalised offers — a potential loyalty and retention feature.
Finding 06
Professional Context
Users want to know what professional profiles frequent a space — a trust signal.
Core Insight
"Users need immediate results on workspace suitability, quick amenity visibility — and verified reviews they can actually trust."
05User Persona — Ivan, 38
Profile
Digital Nomad
Production manager & music festival organizer. From Berlin, relocated to Greece. Irregular hours.
Needs
What Ivan Wants
  • Strong wifi & outlets
  • Large surface for laptop
  • Pet friendly
  • Near other activities
Frustrations
Pain Points
  • Poor wifi signal
  • Fake reviews
  • Unfriendly staff
  • Ugly spaces
06Process & Wireframes
Step 01
User Stories
Research translated into user stories, run in parallel with persona creation.
Step 02
Info Architecture
Structured all content and subcategories. Defined task flows for core objectives.
Step 03
Lo-fi Wireframes
3 tasks: find quiet space, find past café, book for 9 people.
Step 04
Usability Test 1
Remote testing via mic & camera. Led to first design correction cycle.
Step 05
Mid-fi Wireframes
Corrected wireframes based on usability test findings.
Step 06
Hi-fi Prototype
Full interactive prototype with real visual design and complete flows.
